:::{#exm-almost-everywhere}
#### Non-negative except on the integers

Let $g : \reals \to \reals$ with $g(x) = -1$ when $x$ is an integer
and $g(x) = x^2$ otherwise.
The statement "$g(x) \ge 0$" fails exactly for $x \in \mathbb{Z}$,
and $\lebesgue(\mathbb{Z}) = 0$ (@exm-lebesgue-measure),
so $g \ge 0$ holds $\lebesgue$-almost everywhere,
though not everywhere.

For a counting measure, only $\emptyset$ has measure zero (@exm-measure-zero),
so a statement holds almost everywhere only if it holds everywhere.

:::
